trigger_condition: Any authenticated user calls GET /assistants/{id}/shared-with for an assistant they do not own
potential_consequence: User enumeration: grantee list exposed to non-owners

trigger_condition: Any authenticated user calls GET /assistants/{id}/sharable-users for an assistant they do not own
guard_snippet: assistant = Assistant.get_by_id(id_=assistant_id); if not assistant.is_owned_by(user): raise ExtendedHTTPException(code=403, ...)
potential_consequence: Internal user directory searchable by non-owners via any valid assistant ID

trigger_condition: grant() opens a Session block; perm.save() internally opens its own session
guard_snippet: pass session to perm.save(session) or perform insert directly in the outer session
potential_consequence: Two concurrent sessions; permission write may not be visible in the same transaction

trigger_condition: revoke() calls perm.delete() with no session context
guard_snippet: open Session block around the delete loop, pass session to perm.delete(session)
potential_consequence: Each delete uses its own implicit session; partial failures leave stale grants

trigger_condition: POST /share or DELETE /share called with user_ids: [] (empty list)
potential_consequence: No-op call succeeds silently; callers cannot distinguish error from valid empty result

trigger_condition: is_shared_with called when self.id is None (unsaved assistant instance)
potential_consequence: DB query with resource_id=None returns unexpected rows or raises

trigger_condition: per_user_grant_condition uses literal string "assistant" and "user" not enum members
guard_snippet: use ResourceType.ASSISTANT.value and PrincipalType.USER.value or the enum objects directly
potential_consequence: If DB enum stores uppercase labels subquery matches nothing; grants invisible in list queries

trigger_condition: list_shared_with called after user referenced by a Permission row is hard-deleted
guard_snippet: perm.delete() on orphaned rows when db_user is None, or log+skip and return marker
potential_consequence: Orphaned Permission rows silently accumulate; no indication to owner that grant is dangling

trigger_condition: search_sharable_users returns all active users including externals; Python filter applied after DB fetch
guard_snippet: add WHERE user_type != :ext_type inside aquery_active_users or pass user_type filter param
potential_consequence: Large user tables cause unnecessary data transfer; external users visible until Python filter

trigger_condition: Migration new_values=["DATASOURCE", "ASSISTANT"] (uppercase) while Python model declares lowercase values
guard_snippet: align new_values with Python enum values: ["datasource", "assistant"], or verify alembic_postgresql_enum mapping
potential_consequence: Migration may remove existing lowercase datasource rows or add uppercase variant leaving enum inconsistent

trigger_condition: is_global is True AND user.is_external_user is False AND user has a per-user grant on a marketplace assistant
guard_snippet: no change needed if global path always returns True for internal; confirm global assistants cannot have per-user grants (or document intent)
potential_consequence: Per-user grants on global assistants are silently unreachable; grant/revoke endpoints would write orphaned rows

trigger_condition: POST /share called with duplicate user_ids in a single request (same uid appears twice)
potential_consequence: Second iteration hits idempotency check and skips, but DB uniqueness constraint error possible if save() races
